{"parentUuid":"e7819985-b684-45ee-bf01-a824de7b2461","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"ad2aa620ea5ffe0d8","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_014qmMV2eDj1C7fsqypR7yAo","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Prohibited patterns in manuscript prose\n2\t\n3\t**Shared reference. Read on drafting, and read again on review.** The `paper-authoring`\n4\tskill and the `prose-reviewer` agent both consume this file, so a rule cannot mean one\n5\tthing while writing and another while reviewing.\n6\t\n7\t⚠️ **This is the shared FLOOR, not the whole review.** The reviewer additionally carries\n8\treader-outcome questions that do not appear here and that an author must never be given as\n9\ta checklist: a generator optimises against any list it can see. See the skill's §\"Why the\n10\treviewer knows things this file does not\".\n11\t\n12\tEvery rule below was derived from a measured sweep of the 21-bundle corpus, not from a\n13\tstyle guide. Where a number appears, it is what was counted.\n14\t\n15\t---\n16\t\n17\t## 1. The em-dash: prohibited outright, including in headings\n18\t\n19\t**Never write `---` or a literal `—`.** Two forms exist and both are banned.\n20\t\n21\t**Why this one is absolute.** An em-dash reads as machine-authored to a 2026 reader and\n22\tcosts trust before the physics is evaluated. One is as disqualifying as forty, so there is\n23\tno acceptable density. Enforced by `validate.py --check bundle_prose_em_dash_free`, target\n24\tzero. Measured before the corpus was swept: **741 of them, and 0 of 21 bundles clean.**\n25\t\n26\t### ⚠️ The en-dash `--` is MANDATORY and must never be touched\n27\t\n28\t`--` (exactly two hyphens) is a different character doing a different job, and the corpus\n29\tcarries **1,121** of them:\n30\t\n31\t- compound eponyms: `Bose--Einstein`, `Bekenstein--Hawking`, `Schwinger--Keldysh`,\n32\t  `Kaul--Majumdar`, `Chowdhury--Hartnoll--Hebbar--Khondaker`, `SK--EFT`\n33\t- numeric ranges: `pp. 10--15`, `$2$--$3$ K`\n34\t\n35\t**An author over-correcting to \"no dashes at all\" breaks every compound name in the\n36\tprogram, and the check cannot see it** because it counts exactly three hyphens. This is the\n37\tsingle highest-cost mistake available here. One live line contained both:\n38\t`observables---also drives the SK--EFT`.\n39\t\n40\tA third variant exists in the wild: the literal Unicode en-dash `–` (U+2013), found as\n41\t`Kaul–Majumdar` and `Chowdhury–Hartnoll–Hebbar–Khondaker`. Write `--` instead; D3 once\n42\tspelled the same name both ways.\n43\t\n44\t### Replacing an em-dash is a REWRITE, not a substitution\n45\t\n46\tA mechanical swap produces comma splices. Identify the job the dash was doing, then use the\n47\tpunctuation that already exists for that job. Frequencies below are from six independent\n48\treadings of all 741 occurrences.\n49\t\n50\t| The dash was doing | Frequency | Write instead |\n51\t|---|---|---|\n52\t| Paired aside interrupting a clause | ~45–55% | parentheses; a comma pair when the aside is short and contains no commas of its own |\n53\t| Introducing an explanation, expansion or list | ~30–45% | a colon |\n54\t| Separating a label from its gloss in `\\item`, `\\subsection{}`, `\\paragraph{}` | ~15% | a colon, always |\n55\t| Contrastive \"X, not Y\" interjection | ~7% | a comma pair (parentheses would demote a correction to an aside) |\n56\t| Joining two independent clauses | ~3–15% | a semicolon, or a full stop and a new sentence |\n57\t| Trailing appositive glossing a number's significance | common in E1/E2 | a comma |\n58\t\n59\t### The four hard cases, each of which defeats a mechanical fix\n60\t\n61\t1. **The aside contains its own parenthetical or citation.** Converting the outer dash to\n62\t   parentheses yields stacked or nested parens that read as a stutter:\n63\t   `(\\lean{diamondDist_eq_choiSDP}) (the Watrous semidefinite program~\\cite{Watrous2018}) is proven`.\n64\t   **Merge the tag and the aside into ONE parenthetical** with an internal comma or\n65\t   semicolon. Do not nest.\n66\t2. **The aside contains a comma-separated list.** Comma-punctuating it makes the reader\n67\t   parse the inner items as continuing the outer sentence's list. Use parentheses.\n68\t3. **The sentence already has a colon later on.** Adding a second colon reads as a nested\n69\t   label. Restructure with a copula: `X is the headline theorem: Y`.\n70\t4. **Three levels of subordination.** An aside inside an aside inside a main clause is a\n71\t   sentence trying to be three sentences. Split it.\n72\t\n73\t### The generative habits behind them: prohibit these, not just the symbol\n74\t\n75\tAll six readers converged on the same root, so treat it as the rule that matters:\n76\t\n77\t> **Do not interrupt a main clause to insert a clarification.** Write the clarification as\n78\t> its own sentence, before or after.\n79\t\n80\tThe dominant shape was *claim, dash, restatement-with-a-twist, dash, continuation*: draft a\n81\tclean declarative, then, worried a reader will misattribute a convention or miss a caveat,\n82\tsplice the qualifier into the middle. It concentrated in exactly the paragraphs doing the\n83\theaviest epistemic hedging (novelty disclaimers, provenance caveats, convention-pinning),\n84\twhich is where this project's prose is densest.\n85\t\n86\tFour more shapes, each of which reliably produces an em-dash:\n87\t\n88\t- **Name-then-gloss in itemised lists.** `\\item \\verb|foo_bar|: the substantive witness`.\n89\t  Use the colon from the start; this was the single most common pattern in the Lean-heavy\n90\t  bundles.\n91\t- **Label-then-gloss in headings.** `\\subsection{Pillar 1: Golterman--Shamir}`. A dash in a\n92\t  heading also reads as a tic when scanning the table of contents.\n93\t- **Tag-stacking.** A claim ending in a `\\lean{...}` identifier in parens, then a dash\n94\t  glossing that identifier. This is an appositive that got dash-punctuated only because the\n95\t  sentence had already spent its parentheses.\n96\t- **Claim-then-immediately-re-scope.** `T_H \\approx 2.4$ K --- nine orders of magnitude\n97\t  above atomic BEC --- with adiabaticity...`. A defensible instinct for a rigorous program,\n98\t  executed with the wrong punctuation: pick the syntax that matches the qualifier's\n99\t  grammatical role.\n100\t\n101\t---\n102\t\n103\t## 2. A fix may not narrate itself\n104\t\n105\t**Never tell the reader what an earlier draft of this paper said, when it was corrected, or\n106\twhich review round caught it.** A referee has no access to that process and cannot act on\n107\tit; the text reads as a changelog pasted into a manuscript.\n108\t\n109\tEnforced by `validate.py --check bundle_reader_facing_voice`, target zero. Banned forms:\n110\t\n111\t- a correction stamped with a date: `(corrected 2026-08-01)`\n112\t- an account of an earlier draft: `three earlier drafts of this paragraph asserted...`\n113\t- a first-person superseded claim: `We previously shipped a theorem asserting...`\n114\t- an internal review reference: `(D11 Stage-13 round-14 finding 6.2)`\n115\t- the project's own planning documents: `Our earlier planning documents described...`\n116\t- review rounds cast as actors: `rounds 7 and 10 both rated this cosmetic`\n117\t- a claim about the paper's own drafting: `typeset unconditionally in every draft`\n118\t\n119\t**The history is not lost, it moves.** `papers/<X>/change_log.md` and\n120\t`docs/review_finding_supersessions.json` are where a later reader can actually check it, and\n121\tthe ledger entry is required by the lift procedure anyway.\n122\t\n123\t### ⚠️ Removing narration is not deleting content\n124\t\n125\tMost of these passages wrap something real, and the substance must survive:\n126\t\n127\t- **A retraction is a scientific disclosure.** Restate it as a present-tense negative\n128\t  result: what is *not* claimed and why it fails. Do not delete the paragraph.\n129\t- **A scope correction states the correct scope.** Keep every factual statement about what\n130\t  a module does and does not contain, including file:line references. Drop only \"earlier\n131\t  drafts called it X\" and the date/round/finding tag.\n132\t- **A completeness disclaimer is a real caveat.** Keep it; drop the account of what two\n133\t  earlier drafts asserted.\n134\t\n135\t### What is NOT prohibited\n136\t\n137\tReporting that *the literature* corrected something is ordinary scholarship: `Smith\n138\tcorrected this coefficient in 2019` is correct and stays.\n139\t\n140\tDescribing the verification pipeline is legitimate **when the pipeline is the paper's\n141\tsubject matter** (I1, and I2/I3 for library conventions). Addressing the paper's own\n142\treferees is legitimate anywhere: `lets Mathlib4 reviewers calibrate expectations`.\n143\t\n144\tThis distinction is why the rule targets the *act* of self-narration rather than a\n145\tvocabulary. A word list banning `Stage 13`, `reviewer` and `adversarial review` scores 90\n146\thits on this corpus, of which 48 are legitimate uses in the methodology paper alone.\n147\t\n148\t---\n149\t\n150\t## 3. Claim discipline\n151\t\n152\tThese are enforced elsewhere in the pipeline; they are repeated here because they are\n153\tcheaper to satisfy while drafting than to repair at review.\n154\t\n155\t- **Never hedge a count or numerical literal with \"alt convention\" or \"+N depending on\n156\t  convention\" without proving the convention sensitivity.** If counts disagree across\n157\t  tools, find the truth. Convention-drift framing masks actual content drift: a \"161 ± 3\n158\t  alt convention\" was really 164, and the +3 was real drift.\n159\t- **Verify which registry a name lives in before citing it.** `AXIOM_METADATA`,\n160\t  `PLACEHOLDER_THEOREMS`, `HYPOTHESIS_REGISTRY` and `BORDISM_HYPOTHESES` are four different\n161\t  tables; a name found in one and attributed to another is a Stage-13 blocker.\n162\t- **Every cross-language prior-art claim must resolve to a verifiable URL or canonical\n163\t  ecosystem reference.** Hallucinated libraries have shipped before. When in doubt, cite\n164\t  the ecosystem (UniMath, Mathlib4) rather than naming a specific library.\n165\t- **When broadening an attribution, verify every addition belongs in the broadened\n166\t  category.** Surface code is abelian-stabiliser QEC, not non-Abelian-anyon TQC.\n167\t- **Numbers come from the pipeline.** Use `\\input{tables/<spec>.tex}` and the `counts.tex`\n168\t  macros rather than typing a literal.\n169\t\n170\t---\n171\t\n172\t## 4. Structure\n173\t\n174\t- **The abstract leads with the result**, not with the programme, the architecture, or what\n175\t  the paper will do.\n176\t- **The reader never sees the project's internal taxonomy.** Not `bundle`, `tier`, `wave`,\n177\t  `phase`, or `splash`. Companion papers are cited as papers, by title, in a normal\n178\t  reference list. This is what makes a manuscript read as a repository index: F's organising\n179\t  vocabulary was its own publication plan.\n180\t- **Section architecture is authored, not accumulated.** A bundle's sections come from its\n181\t  charter, written before any source is registered. Do not add a section because a source\n182\t  was registered: D3 has 37 sections against 31 sources, which is sedimentation.\n183\t- **Every figure is planned.** A bundle with no figures is a charter defect, not a style\n184\t  choice; 9 of 21 bundles shipped zero figures because the lift step only ever *migrated*\n185\t  figures that already existed.\n186\t"}]},"uuid":"bebfde81-4b99-4ff6-b2c2-7afd51435991","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:36:54.863Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"e7819985-b684-45ee-bf01-a824de7b2461","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

Provides the house voice, the prohibited-pattern floor, and venue conventions for SK-EFT Hawking publication bundles.\n4\t---\n5\t\n6\t# Authoring a publication bundle\n7\t\n8\tGuidance for writing manuscript prose in `papers/<bundle>/paper_draft.tex`. This is the\n9\tgenerative counterpart to the `prose-reviewer` agent; both read the same prohibited-pattern\n10\treference so a rule cannot drift between writing and review.\n11\t\n12\tRead it either way you draft: the lead writing in-context, or a `paper-drafter` agent\n13\tdispatched over one section. `paper-drafter` reads this file and the same reference by\n14\tpath, so the floor is identical however the prose is produced.\n15\t\n16\t**Read `references/prohibited-patterns.md` before drafting.** It is mandatory, not\n17\tbackground, and it is short.\n18\t\n19\t---\n20\t\n21\t## Why this skill exists\n22\t\n23\tThe pipeline had three reviewer agents and no authoring guidance. Everything about how to\n24\twrite lived in `docs/BUNDLE_LIFT_PROCEDURE.md` §7 as a bookkeeping checklist consulted at\n25\tlift time. The measured result of that gap, across 21 bundles:\n26\t\n27\t- **741 em-dashes**, with zero bundles clean\n28\t- **13 passages** narrating the paper's own correction history to a referee\n29\t- **9 of 21 bundles shipping zero figures**, because the lift step only migrated figures\n30\t  that already existed and no step ever planned one\n31\t- **D3 carrying 37 sections against 31 contributing sources**, which is sedimentation\n32\t  rather than architecture\n33\t\n34\tNone of that is a capability limit. It is what an unguided generator produces when the only\n35\tcontrols are downstream reviewers.\n36\t\n37\t---\n38\t\n39\t## Before writing a section\n40\t\n41\t1. **Read the charter.** `papers/<X>/bundle_metadata.json` carries `target_journal` and\n42\t   `length_target`; the section belongs to a planned outline, not to a source paper that\n43\t   happened to be registered.\n44\t2. **Read the substrate directly.** Contributing per-paper drafts, the Lean modules, the\n45\t   roadmap. Do not write from a summary.\n46\t3. **Know the claim this section makes** and which apex theorem backs it. A section whose\n47\t   claim has no Lean witness is a finding waiting to happen.\n48\t\n49\t## While writing\n50\t\n51\tWrite for a referee at the named venue who has never seen the repository, cannot run the\n52\tcode, and will not read a second sentence to understand the first.\n53\t\n54\t- **State the result, then support it.** Not the programme, not the architecture, not what\n55\t  the section will do.\n56\t- **One clause, one job.** Do not interrupt a main clause to insert a clarification; write\n57\t  the clarification as its own sentence. This single habit produced most of the corpus's\n58\t  em-dashes.\n59\t- **No em-dash, ever** (`---` or `—`). **`--` is mandatory** for compound eponyms and\n60\t  ranges and must never be touched. Both rules and every replacement case are in\n61\t  `references/prohibited-patterns.md` §1; read them before reaching for a dash.\n62\t- **A fix never narrates itself.** Correct silently in the manuscript and record the history\n63\t  in `change_log.md` and the supersession ledger (§2 of the reference).\n64\t- **Numbers come from the pipeline** via `\\input{tables/<spec>.tex}` and the `counts.tex`\n65\t  macros, never typed as literals.\n66\t- **Cite companion work as papers**, by title. The reader never sees `bundle`, `tier`,\n67\t  `wave`, `phase` or `splash`.\n68\t\n69\t## Before handing off\n70\t\n71\t```bash\n72\tuv run python scripts/compile_bundle_pdf.py <X>   # must be clean\n73\tuv run python scripts/validate.py \\\n74\t    --check bundle_prose_em_dash_free \\\n75\t    --check bundle_reader_facing_voice \\\n76\t    --check bundle_manuscript_length\n77\t```\n78\t\n79\tCompile through `compile_bundle_pdf.py`, never `pdflatex` inside `papers/<X>/`. An in-place\n80\tcompile clobbers `paper_draft.{aux,log,synctex.gz}`, and a reviewer running concurrently then\n81\tjudges your draft by a `.log` that belongs to someone else's pass.\n82\t\n83\tAll three are deterministic and all three must pass. They are a floor, not a review: they\n84\tconfirm nothing prohibited is present, and say nothing about whether the argument carries.\n85\t\n86\t---\n87\t\n88\t## Why the reviewer knows things this file does not\n89\t\n90\tThe `prose-reviewer` agent reads this same reference, so the two never disagree about a\n91\trule. It also carries a brief that is deliberately **not** written down here, framed on\n92\treader outcome rather than rule compliance: where a reader would stop, whether the abstract\n93\tleads with the result, whether each section advances a single argument.\n94\t\n95\tThat asymmetry is intentional. A generator optimises against any checklist it can see, so a\n96\treviewer briefed entirely off the author's rules would pass anything the author produced.\n97\tSatisfying this file is necessary and not sufficient.\n98\t\n99\t---\n100\t\n101\t## Additional resources\n102\t\n103\t### Reference files\n104\t\n105\t- **`references/prohibited-patterns.md`** — mandatory read. The em-dash prohibition and its\n106\t  replacement cases, the self-narration ban, claim discipline, structure rules. Shared with\n107\t  the `prose-reviewer` agent.\n108\t\n109\t### Related surfaces\n110\t\n111\t- `docs/BUNDLE_LIFT_PROCEDURE.md` — the 14-step lift workflow this drafting sits inside\n112\t  (§7 authoring, §11 the BLOCKER loop, §12a the terminal de-scarring pass).\n113\t- `docs/WAVE_EXECUTION_PIPELINE.md` Stage 10 — the process law and its gates.\n114\t- `docs/BUNDLE_DIRECTORY_SCHEMA.md` — `length_target`, `apex_theorems`, and who writes what.\n115\t"}]},"uuid":"207f02de-4c16-4e9b-9350-275b4dfc0d37","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:37:07.903Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f1fb8741-28c7-4c7b-87c9-261ccae15ce9","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

Formalizes gravitational-wave propagation speed and\n11\tthe leading dispersion correction in terms of the vestigial-phase\n12\tmetric-channel susceptibility `χ_vest` and a dissipative coefficient\n13\t`γ`.\n14\t\n15\t⚠️ **Both are FREE PARAMETERS of this module — it has no project\n16\tdependencies, by design.** `χ_vest` is a free `ℝ` in `c_GW`; `γ` is a\n17\tfree `ℝ` in `dispersion_correction`. The prose counterparts\n18\t`VestigialSusceptibility.chi_RPA` and `SecondOrderSK.GammaH` are the\n19\tsubstrate's *models* for these quantities, not values it computes:\n20\t`chi_RPA χ₀ γ⋆ = χ₀ / (1 − γ⋆ * χ₀)` is a resummation of the bubble\n21\tintegral `χ₀` (the two are distinct), and neither `χ₀` nor `γ⋆` is\n22\tevaluated anywhere in the project. So this module IMPORTS neither, and\n23\tmust not be described as deriving `χ_vest` from them. What it does is\n24\tCONSTRAIN `χ_vest` against a datum — see `Key Results` 4.\n25\t(review:2026-08-14-l1-stage13:L1:3.2)\n26\t\n27\tThe correctness-push anchor is the GW170817 multi-messenger bound\n28\t`|c_GW − c| / c ≤ 3 × 10⁻¹⁵` (Abbott et al. ApJL 848, L13 (2017)).\n29\t\n30\t**Phase 5y H1 caveat (LOAD-BEARING).** The Phase 5y H1 deep research\n31\tfinding (`Lit-Search/Phase-5y/Phase 5y Hypothesis 1 — Kronecker-Anomaly Second-Sound Graviton as Dark Energy Candidate.md`)\n32\testablished that the second-sound mode is NOT derived as a propagating\n33\tDOF from first principles — the Volovik identification \"second sound =\n34\tgraviton\" is an *identification*, not a derivation. Wave 2 ships in\n35\t\"use-as-identified\" mode with the bridge encoded as a tracked-hypothesis\n36\tProp `H_VestigialModeIsGraviton`. The module's main physical content\n37\tis a *quantitative constraint*: GW170817 confines `χ_vest` to the\n38\twindow `[(1−τ)², (1+τ)²]` with `τ = tolGW170817 = 3 × 10⁻¹⁵`. That\n39\twindow lies strictly INSIDE the natural range `[0.1, 10]` — the two\n40\tare nested, not disjoint, and they share `χ_vest = 1` — and it is\n41\tnarrower than the natural range by more than 14 orders of magnitude.\n42\tSo the datum pins the parameter to unity rather than excluding the\n43\trange: the ENDPOINTS `χ_vest = 0.1, 10` are excluded; `χ_vest = 1`\n44\tis not. The `|Δc/c|` values `0.68` and `2.16` are the deviations at\n45\tthose two endpoints, not over the range.\n46\t\n47\t## Key Results\n48\t\n49\t1. **GW propagation speed.** `c_GW χ_vest c = c · √χ_vest`, with\n50\t   `χ_vest = 1` recovering `c_GW = c` exactly.\n51\t2. **Deviation formula.** `Δc/c (χ_vest) = √χ_vest − 1`; vanishes\n52\t   iff `χ_vest = 1`.\n53\t3. **GW170817 correctness-push.** Predicate `LigoSatisfied δ tol`\n54\t   captures `|δ| ≤ tol`. Biconditional\n55\t   `c_GW_match_iff_chi_close_to_one` characterises the\n56\t   c_GW = c locus.\n57\t4. **Natural-range endpoints excluded; interior constrained\n58\t   (LOAD-BEARING).** The ENDPOINTS of\n59\t   `[CHI_VEST_NATURAL_LOWER, CHI_VEST_NATURAL_UPPER] = [0.1, 10]`\n60\t   produce deviations vastly exceeding the GW170817 cap\n61\t   (`natural_lower_violates_ligo`, `natural_upper_violates_ligo`),\n62\t   while `ligo_confines_chi_vest_within_natural_range` shows every\n63\t   LIGO-compatible `χ_vest` lies strictly interior to that range, and\n64\t   `ligo_window_subset_natural_range` shows the compatible window is\n65\t   nested inside it.\n66\t5. **Bundled tracked hypothesis.** `H_VestigialModeIsGraviton` records\n67\t   the Volovik-Phase 5y H1 identification together with a\n68\t   constraint that `χ_vest` lies in a sub-window of the natural range\n69\t   compatible with GW170817. The bundle is genuinely non-trivial:\n70\t   it is satisfiable at `χ_vest = 1` and each conjunct has an explicit\n71\t   falsifier.\n72\t7. **`c`-independence, proved.** `c_GW_relative_deviation_eq` shows\n73\t   `(c_GW χ c − c)/c = c_GW_deviation χ` for every `c ≠ 0`, tying the\n74\t   `c`-free deviation formula back to `c_GW` itself.\n75\t6. **Dispersion correction.** `dispersion_correction γ ω = γ · ω`\n76\t   captures the leading SK-EFT/Γ_H dissipative correction; vanishes\n77\t   when γ = 0.\n78\t\n79\t## Conventions\n80\t\n81\t- Natural units: `c = 1` (SI factor restored only at the\n82\t  observational-bound layer).\n83\t- `χ_vest` is the dimensionless metric-channel susceptibility\n84\t  (in units of inverse Λ²); `χ_vest = 1` is the natural anchor.\n85\t- The deviation `δ = Δc/c = √χ_vest − 1` is dimensionless and\n86\t  signed.\n87\t- GW170817 cap: `tolGW170817 = 3e-15` (symmetric two-sided cap).\n88\t\n89\t## References\n90\t\n91\t- Abbott et al. (LIGO+Virgo+EM partners), \"Gravitational Waves and\n92\t  Gamma-Rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and\n93\t  GRB 170817A\", ApJL 848, L13 (2017).\n94\t- Volovik, \"Fermionic quartet and vestigial gravity\", JETP Lett. 119,\n95\t  330 (2024); DOI 10.1134/S002136402460006X. NOTE: this paper does NOT\n96\t  contain the second-sound--graviton identification; that is advanced in\n97\t  arXiv:2601.00639 and arXiv:2410.04392, where Volovik derives `s₂ = c`\n98\t  exactly and notes it is GW170817-compatible.\n99\t- Phase 5y H1 deep research,\n100\t  `Lit-Search/Phase-5y/Phase 5y Hypothesis 1 — Kronecker-Anomaly Second-Sound Graviton as Dark Energy Candidate.md`.\n101\t- Crossley-Glorioso-Liu, \"Effective field theory of dissipative\n102\t  fluids\", JHEP 2017 (arXiv:1511.03646).\n103\t- VestigialSusceptibility.lean (`chi_RPA` closed form).\n104\t- SecondOrderSK.lean (`GammaH` transport identification).\n105\t- LinearizedEFE.lean (Phase 6a Wave 1).\n106\t-/\n107\t\n108\tnamespace SKEFTHawking.GravitationalWaves\n109\t\n110\topen Real\n111\t\n112\t/-! ## 1. GW propagation speed from vestigial susceptibility -/\n113\t\n114\t/-- Gravitational-wave propagation speed from the vestigial-phase\n115\t    metric-channel susceptibility `χ_vest` and the speed of light `c`:\n116\t\n117\t      `c_GW χ_vest c = c · √χ_vest`.\n118\t\n119\t    This is the leading-order identification under\n120\t    `H_VestigialModeIsGraviton` (Volovik 2024 + Phase 5y H1\n121\t    \"use-as-identified\" mode). The natural anchor `χ_vest = 1`\n122\t    gives `c_GW = c`. -/\n123\tnoncomputable def c_GW (χ_vest c : ℝ) : ℝ := c * Real.sqrt χ_vest\n124\t\n125\t/-- At the natural anchor `χ_vest = 1`, GW speed equals light speed. -/\n126\ttheorem c_GW_at_chi_one (c : ℝ) : c_GW 1 c = c := by\n127\t  unfold c_GW\n128\t  simp\n129\t\n130\t/-- For positive `χ_vest` and positive `c`, `c_GW` is strictly positive. -/\n131\ttheorem c_GW_pos {χ_vest c : ℝ} (hχ : 0 < χ_vest) (hc : 0 < c) :\n132\t    0 < c_GW χ_vest c := by\n133\t  unfold c_GW\n134\t  exact mul_pos hc (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hχ)\n135\t\n136\t/-- Dimensionless GW-speed deviation from light:\n137\t    `Δc/c (χ_vest) = √χ_vest − 1`. Independent of `c`. -/\n138\tnoncomputable def c_GW_deviation (χ_vest : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.sqrt χ_vest - 1\n139\t\n140\t/-- **Bridge: `c_GW_deviation` IS the relative deviation of `c_GW`.** For any\n141\t    `c ≠ 0`,\n142\t\n143\t      `(c_GW χ_vest c − c) / c = c_GW_deviation χ_vest`.\n144\t\n145\t    This is what makes the `c`-independence of `c_GW_deviation` a proved\n146\t    fact rather than a definitional convention: the right-hand side has no\n147\t    `c` in it, so the measured fractional speed offset is the same for\n148\t    every non-zero `c`. Every GW170817 theorem below is stated in terms of\n149\t    `c_GW_deviation`, and this lemma is what ties those statements back to\n150\t    `c_GW`. -/\n151\ttheorem c_GW_relative_deviation_eq {χ_vest c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) :\n152\t    (c_GW χ_vest c - c) / c = c_GW_deviation χ_vest := by\n153\t  unfold c_GW c_GW_deviation\n154\t  rw [div_eq_iff hc]\n155\t  ring\n156\t\n157\t/-- The deviation vanishes iff `χ_vest = 1`. -/\n158\ttheorem c_GW_deviation_zero_iff_chi_one {χ_vest : ℝ} (hχ : 0 ≤ χ_vest) :\n159\t    c_GW_deviation χ_vest = 0 ↔ χ_vest = 1 := by\n160\t  unfold c_GW_deviation\n161\t  constructor\n162\t  · intro h\n163\t    have hsqrt : Real.sqrt χ_vest = 1 := by linarith\n164\t    have : Real.sqrt χ_vest * Real.sqrt χ_vest = 1 * 1 := by\n165\t      rw [hsqrt]\n166\t    rw [Real.mul_self_sqrt hχ] at this\n167\t    linarith\n168\t  · intro h\n169\t    rw [h]; simp\n170\t\n171\t/-- The deviation is monotonically increasing in `χ_vest` on `[0, ∞)`.\n172\t    Strict monotonicity follows from strict monotonicity of `Real.sqrt`. -/\n173\ttheorem c_GW_deviation_strict_mono :\n174\t    StrictMonoOn c_GW_deviation (Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)) := by\n175\t  intro a ha b hb hab\n176\t  unfold c_GW_deviation\n177\t  have : Real.sqrt a < Real.sqrt b := by\n178\t    exact Real.sqrt_lt_sqrt ha hab\n179\t  linarith\n180\t\n181\t/-! ## 2. GW170817 correctness-push -/\n182\t\n183\t/-- Symmetric two-sided GW170817 cap (Abbott et al. ApJL 848, L13 (2017),\n184\t    Eq. (5)): `|c_GW − c|/c ≤ 3 × 10⁻¹⁵`. -/\n185\tnoncomputable def tolGW170817 : ℝ := 3e-15\n186\t\n187\t/-- The GW170817 constraint as a predicate on the deviation. -/\n188\tdef LigoSatisfied (δ : ℝ) : Prop := |δ| ≤ tolGW170817\n189\t\n190\t/-- The natural anchor `χ_vest = 1` exactly satisfies the GW170817 cap\n191\t    (deviation = 0). This is the \"if χ = 1 then OK\" half. -/\n192\ttheorem ligo_satisfied_at_chi_one : LigoSatisfied (c_GW_deviation 1) := by\n193\t  unfold LigoSatisfied\n194\t  rw [c_GW_deviation, Real.sqrt_one]\n195\t  simp [tolGW170817]\n196\t  norm_num\n197\t\n198\t/-- **Correctness-push biconditional.** For `χ_vest ∈ (0, ∞)`,\n199\t    `LigoSatisfied (Δc/c)` iff `χ_vest` lies inside the\n200\t    `[(1 − tol)², (1 + tol)²]` square of the GW170817 tolerance. -/\n201\ttheorem c_GW_match_iff_chi_close_to_one {χ_vest : ℝ} (hχ : 0 ≤ χ_vest) :\n202\t    LigoSatisfied (c_GW_deviation χ_vest) ↔\n203\t      (1 - tolGW170817)^2 ≤ χ_vest ∧ χ_vest ≤ (1 + tolGW170817)^2 := by\n204\t  unfold LigoSatisfied c_GW_deviation\n205\t  have h_tol_pos : 0 < tolGW170817 := by unfold tolGW170817; norm_num\n206\t  have h_tol_lt_one : tolGW170817 < 1 := by unfold tolGW170817; norm_num\n207\t  have h_one_minus_tol_nn : 0 ≤ 1 - tolGW170817 := by linarith\n208\t  have h_one_plus_tol_nn : 0 ≤ 1 + tolGW170817 := by linarith\n209\t  have hsqrt_nn : 0 ≤ Real.sqrt χ_vest := Real.sqrt_nonneg _\n210\t  have hsq_eq : (Real.sqrt χ_vest)^2 = χ_vest := Real.sq_sqrt hχ\n211\t  rw [abs_le]\n212\t  constructor\n213\t  · rintro ⟨h_lo, h_hi⟩\n214\t    have h_sqrt_lo : 1 - tolGW170817 ≤ Real.sqrt χ_vest := by linarith\n215\t    have h_sqrt_hi : Real.sqrt χ_vest ≤ 1 + tolGW170817 := by linarith\n216\t    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n217\t    · nlinarith [sq_nonneg (Real.sqrt χ_vest - (1 - tolGW170817)), hsq_eq]\n218\t    · nlinarith [sq_nonneg ((1 + tolGW170817) - Real.sqrt χ_vest), hsq_eq]\n219\t  · rintro ⟨h_lo, h_hi⟩\n220\t    have h_sqrt_lo : 1 - tolGW170817 ≤ Real.sqrt χ_vest := by\n221\t      have h1 : Real.sqrt ((1 - tolGW170817)^2) ≤ Real.sqrt χ_vest :=\n222\t        Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h_lo\n223\t      rwa [Real.sqrt_sq h_one_minus_tol_nn] at h1\n224\t    have h_sqrt_hi : Real.sqrt χ_vest ≤ 1 + tolGW170817 := by\n225\t      have h1 : Real.sqrt χ_vest ≤ Real.sqrt ((1 + tolGW170817)^2) :=\n226\t        Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h_hi\n227\t      rwa [Real.sqrt_sq h_one_plus_tol_nn] at h1\n228\t    constructor <;> linarith\n229\t\n230\t/-! ## 3. Natural-range endpoints and the GW170817 constraint (LOAD-BEARING)\n231\t\n232\t    The vestigial-susceptibility \"natural range\" is `χ_vest · Λ² ∈ [0.1, 10]`\n233\t    (a half-decade window, matching `GRAV.ALPHA_ADW_LOWER/UPPER`). At\n234\t    either END of this range the GW deviation `Δc/c` exceeds the GW170817\n235\t    cap by 14+ orders of magnitude.\n236\t\n237\t    The GW170817-compatible window `[(1−τ)², (1+τ)²]`, `τ = tolGW170817`,\n238\t    is **nested strictly inside** the natural range — not disjoint from it\n239\t    (`ligo_window_subset_natural_range`), and it contains the natural\n240\t    anchor `χ_vest = 1`. So the Wave 2 result is a fine-tuning\n241\t    CONSTRAINT, not an exclusion of the range: GW170817 pins `χ_vest` to\n242\t    within `~3e-15` of unity, a window narrower than the natural range by\n243\t    more than 14 orders of magnitude\n244\t    (`ligo_window_width_lt_natural_range_width_by_1e14`).\n245\t-/\n246\t\n247\t/-- Natural-range lower bound: `χ_vest^L = 0.1` (matches\n248\t    `GW.CHI_VEST_NATURAL_LOWER` in constants.py). -/\n249\tnoncomputable def chi_vest_natural_lower : ℝ := 1 / 10\n250\t\n251\t/-- Natural-range upper bound: `χ_vest^U = 10`. -/\n252\tnoncomputable def chi_vest_natural_upper : ℝ := 10\n253\t\n254\t/-- **Lower-end falsifier.** At `χ_vest = 1/10`, the deviation\n255\t    `Δc/c = √(1/10) − 1 ≈ −0.684` exceeds `tolGW170817 = 3e-15`. -/\n256\ttheorem natural_lower_violates_ligo :\n257\t    ¬ LigoSatisfied (c_GW_deviation chi_vest_natural_lower) := by\n258\t  unfold LigoSatisfied c_GW_deviation chi_vest_natural_lower tolGW170817\n259\t  intro habs\n260\t  rw [abs_le] at habs\n261\t  obtain ⟨h_lo, _⟩ := habs\n262\t  -- h_lo : -3e-15 ≤ sqrt(1/10) - 1\n263\t  -- Use sqrt(1/10) ≤ sqrt(1/4) = 1/2\n264\t  have h_le_quarter : (1 : ℝ) / 10 ≤ 1 / 4 := by norm_num\n265\t  have h_sqrt : Real.sqrt (1 / 10) ≤ Real.sqrt (1 / 4) :=\n266\t    Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h_le_quarter\n267\t  have h_quarter : Real.sqrt (1 / 4 : ℝ) = 1 / 2 := by\n268\t    rw [show (1 / 4 : ℝ) = (1 / 2 : ℝ)^2 by norm_num]\n269\t    exact Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num)\n270\t  rw [h_quarter] at h_sqrt\n271\t  -- So sqrt(0.1) - 1 ≤ 0.5 - 1 = -0.5, much less than -3e-15\n272\t  linarith\n273\t\n274\t/-- **Upper-end falsifier.** At `χ_vest = 10`, the deviation\n275\t    `Δc/c = √10 − 1 ≈ 2.162` exceeds `tolGW170817 = 3e-15`. -/\n276\ttheorem natural_upper_violates_ligo :\n277\t    ¬ LigoSatisfied (c_GW_deviation chi_vest_natural_upper) := by\n278\t  unfold LigoSatisfied c_GW_deviation chi_vest_natural_upper tolGW170817\n279\t  intro habs\n280\t  rw [abs_le] at habs\n281\t  obtain ⟨_, h_hi⟩ := habs\n282\t  -- h_hi : sqrt(10) - 1 ≤ 3e-15\n283\t  -- sqrt(10) ≥ sqrt(4) = 2\n284\t  have h_ge_four : (4 : ℝ) ≤ 10 := by norm_num\n285\t  have h_sqrt : Real.sqrt 4 ≤ Real.sqrt 10 := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h_ge_four\n286\t  have h_four : Real.sqrt (4 : ℝ) = 2 := by\n287\t    rw [show (4 : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ)^2 by norm_num]\n288\t    exact Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num)\n289\t  rw [h_four] at h_sqrt\n290\t  -- sqrt(10) - 1 ≥ 2 - 1 = 1, much greater than 3e-15\n291\t  linarith\n292\t\n293\t/-- **Bundled endpoint falsifier.** Both endpoints of the natural χ_vest\n294\t    range fail the GW170817 constraint.\n295\t\n296\t    This is a statement about the two ENDPOINTS. The range as a whole is\n297\t    not excluded: it contains `χ_vest = 1`, which satisfies the cap\n298\t    (`ligo_satisfied_at_chi_one`). The compatible sub-window is located by\n299\t    `ligo_confines_chi_vest_within_natural_range`. -/\n300\ttheorem vestigial_natural_range_violates_ligo :\n301\t    ¬ LigoSatisfied (c_GW_deviation chi_vest_natural_lower) ∧\n302\t    ¬ LigoSatisfied (c_GW_deviation chi_vest_natural_upper) :=\n303\t  ⟨natural_lower_violates_ligo, natural_upper_violates_ligo⟩\n304\t\n305\t/-! ### 3.1 The GW170817-compatible window, located and measured\n306\t\n307\t    `c_GW_match_iff_chi_close_to_one` characterises the compatible set as\n308\t    `[(1−τ)², (1+τ)²]`. The results here say *where* that interval sits\n309\t    relative to the natural range, and *how wide* it is. -/\n310\t\n311\t/-- The natural lower bound lies strictly below the compatible window. -/\n312\ttheorem natural_lower_lt_ligo_window_lower :\n313\t    chi_vest_natural_lower < (1 - tolGW170817) ^ 2 := by\n314\t  unfold chi_vest_natural_lower tolGW170817\n315\t  norm_num\n316\t\n317\t/-- The compatible window's upper end lies strictly below the natural upper bound. -/\n318\ttheorem ligo_window_upper_lt_natural_upper :\n319\t    (1 + tolGW170817) ^ 2 < chi_vest_natural_upper := by\n320\t  unfold chi_vest_natural_upper tolGW170817\n321\t  norm_num\n322\t\n323\t/-- **The compatible window is nested inside the natural range.** The\n324\t    GW170817-compatible set `[(1−τ)², (1+τ)²]` is a subset of the natural\n325\t    range `[0.1, 10]` — the two are NOT disjoint. -/\n326\ttheorem ligo_window_subset_natural_range :\n327\t    Set.Icc ((1 - tolGW170817) ^ 2) ((1 + tolGW170817) ^ 2) ⊆\n328\t      Set.Icc chi_vest_natural_lower chi_vest_natural_upper := by\n329\t  intro x hx\n330\t  exact ⟨le_of_lt (lt_of_lt_of_le natural_lower_lt_ligo_window_lower hx.1),\n331\t    le_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt hx.2 ligo_window_upper_lt_natural_upper)⟩\n332\t\n333\t/-- The natural anchor `χ_vest = 1` lies in the compatible window. Together\n334\t    with `ligo_window_subset_natural_range` this witnesses that the window\n335\t    is non-empty, so the confinement theorem below is not vacuous. -/\n336\ttheorem chi_one_mem_ligo_window :\n337\t    (1 : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc ((1 - tolGW170817) ^ 2) ((1 + tolGW170817) ^ 2) :=\n338\t  (c_GW_match_iff_chi_close_to_one zero_le_one).mp ligo_satisfied_at_chi_one\n339\t\n340\t/-- **The compatible window and the natural range intersect.** They share\n341\t    `χ_vest = 1`. This is the explicit refutation of any claim that the\n342\t    natural range and the GW170817-compatible window are disjoint: the\n343\t    correct relation is nesting (`ligo_window_subset_natural_range`). -/\n344\ttheorem ligo_window_inter_natural_range_nonempty :\n345\t    (Set.Icc ((1 - tolGW170817) ^ 2) ((1 + tolGW170817) ^ 2) ∩\n346\t      Set.Icc chi_vest_natural_lower chi_vest_natural_upper).Nonempty :=\n347\t  ⟨1, chi_one_mem_ligo_window, ligo_window_subset_natural_range chi_one_mem_ligo_window⟩\n348\t\n349\t/-- **Headline constraint.** GW170817 confines `χ_vest` to a narrow\n350\t    interval about unity that lies strictly interior to the natural range.\n351\t\n352\t    For non-negative `χ_vest` satisfying the LIGO cap: `χ_vest` lies in\n353\t    `[(1−τ)², (1+τ)²]`, and hence strictly between the natural bounds\n354\t    `0.1` and `10`.\n355\t\n356\t    This is a CONSTRAINT, not a falsification. The datum pins the\n357\t    parameter to unity; it does not exclude the natural range, which\n358\t    contains the pinned value (`chi_one_mem_ligo_window`). -/\n359\ttheorem ligo_confines_chi_vest_within_natural_range {χ_vest : ℝ} (hχ : 0 ≤ χ_vest)\n360\t    (hligo : LigoSatisfied (c_GW_deviation χ_vest)) :\n361\t    (1 - tolGW170817) ^ 2 ≤ χ_vest ∧ χ_vest ≤ (1 + tolGW170817) ^ 2 ∧\n362\t      chi_vest_natural_lower < χ_vest ∧ χ_vest < chi_vest_natural_upper := by\n363\t  obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := (c_GW_match_iff_chi_close_to_one hχ).mp hligo\n364\t  exact ⟨hlo, hhi, lt_of_lt_of_le natural_lower_lt_ligo_window_lower hlo,\n365\t    lt_of_le_of_lt hhi ligo_window_upper_lt_natural_upper⟩\n366\t\n367\t/-- **Window width.** `(1+τ)² − (1−τ)² = 4τ` exactly. -/\n368\ttheorem ligo_window_width_eq :\n369\t    (1 + tolGW170817) ^ 2 - (1 - tolGW170817) ^ 2 = 4 * tolGW170817 := by\n370\t  ring\n371\t\n372\t/-- **Window width, absolute bound.** With `τ = 3e-15` the compatible\n373\t    window is narrower than `1e-13`. -/\n374\ttheorem ligo_window_width_lt_1e13 :\n375\t    (1 + tolGW170817) ^ 2 - (1 - tolGW170817) ^ 2 < 1e-13 := by\n376\t  rw [ligo_window_width_eq]\n377\t  unfold tolGW170817\n378\t  norm_num\n379\t\n380\t/-- **Natural-range width.** `10 − 0.1 = 9.9`. -/\n381\ttheorem natural_range_width_eq :\n382\t    chi_vest_natural_upper - chi_vest_natural_lower = 99 / 10 := by\n383\t  unfold chi_vest_natural_upper chi_vest_natural_lower\n384\t  norm_num\n385\t\n386\t/-- **The fine-tuning, quantified.** Scaling the compatible window up by\n387\t    `10¹⁴` still leaves it narrower than the natural range. This is the\n388\t    falsifiable form of \"GW170817 fine-tunes `χ_vest` by more than 14\n389\t    orders of magnitude\": the constraint shrinks the admissible interval\n390\t    from width `9.9` to width `4τ = 1.2e-14`. -/\n391\ttheorem ligo_window_width_lt_natural_range_width_by_1e14 :\n392\t    1e14 * ((1 + tolGW170817) ^ 2 - (1 - tolGW170817) ^ 2) <\n393\t      chi_vest_natural_upper - chi_vest_natural_lower := by\n394\t  rw [ligo_window_width_eq, natural_range_width_eq]\n395\t  unfold tolGW170817\n396\t  norm_num\n397\t\n398\t/-! ## 4. Tracked-hypothesis: vestigial mode = graviton (Phase 5y H1)\n399\t\n400\t    What the GW170817 datum settles about the Volovik identification\n401\t    splits into two halves, and the theorems here keep them apart.\n402\t\n403\t    *Negative half* — `natural_endpoints_violate_ligo_window` and\n404\t    `natural_endpoints_violate_ligo_for_every_c`: the two ENDPOINTS of\n405\t    the natural range are excluded, and no choice of the speed of light\n406\t    `c` rescues them, because the relative deviation of `c_GW` equals\n407\t    `c_GW_deviation χ` for every `c ≠ 0` (`c_GW_relative_deviation_eq`).\n408\t    Both are two-point statements about `χ = 0.1` and `χ = 10`; neither\n409\t    says anything about interior values.\n410\t\n411\t    *Positive half* — §3.1: the compatible window is non-empty, contains\n412\t    `χ = 1`, and is nested strictly inside the natural range. The natural\n413\t    range is therefore CONSTRAINED, not excluded.\n414\t\n415\t    `H_VestigialModeIsGraviton` bundles the identification as\n416\t    P1 (`χ_vest > 0`) ∧ P2 (GW170817 cap) ∧ P3' (`|Δc/c| < 1/2`).\n417\t    P3' is not implied by P1: `χ_vest = 1/4` satisfies P1 and fails P3'\n418\t    at exactly `|Δ| = 1/2`.\n419\t-/\n420\t\n421\t/-- **Endpoint exclusion.** No `χ` equal to either endpoint of the natural\n422\t    range `[chi_vest_natural_lower, chi_vest_natural_upper] = [0.1, 10]`\n423\t    satisfies the GW170817 cap.\n424\t\n425\t    This is a TWO-POINT statement, about `χ = 0.1` and `χ = 10` only. The\n426\t    interior of the natural range is governed by\n427\t    `ligo_confines_chi_vest_within_natural_range`, which locates the\n428\t    compatible sub-interval about `χ = 1`. -/\n429\ttheorem natural_endpoints_violate_ligo_window :\n430\t    ¬ ∃ χ : ℝ,\n431\t      (χ = chi_vest_natural_lower ∨ χ = chi_vest_natural_upper) ∧\n432\t      LigoSatisfied (c_GW_deviation χ) := by\n433\t  rintro ⟨χ, hcase, hligo⟩\n434\t  rcases hcase with h | h\n435\t  · rw [h] at hligo; exact natural_lower_violates_ligo hligo\n436\t  · rw [h] at hligo; exact natural_upper_violates_ligo hligo\n437\t\n438\t/-- **Endpoint exclusion holds for every speed of light.** For any\n439\t    `c ≠ 0`, the measured relative deviation `(c_GW χ c − c) / c` at either\n440\t    natural-range endpoint violates the GW170817 cap.\n441\t\n442\t    The `c` binder is load-bearing here: the statement is about the\n443\t    relative deviation of `c_GW` itself, and it reduces to the\n444\t    `c`-free `c_GW_deviation χ` only through\n445\t    `c_GW_relative_deviation_eq`. So no UV rescaling of the speed of\n446\t    light converts an endpoint value of `χ` into a compatible one. -/\n447\ttheorem natural_endpoints_violate_ligo_for_every_c\n448\t    {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) {χ : ℝ}\n449\t    (hχ : χ = chi_vest_natural_lower ∨ χ = chi_vest_natural_upper) :\n450\t    ¬ LigoSatisfied ((c_GW χ c - c) / c) := by\n451\t  rw [c_GW_relative_deviation_eq hc]\n452\t  rcases hχ with h | h\n453\t  · rw [h]; load-bearing, NOT implied by P1\n465\t          since e.g. χ_vest = 1/10 gives Δ ≈ -0.684 which violates\n466\t          P3' even though χ > 0)\n467\t\n468\t    The bundle is genuinely non-trivial: explicit falsifiers below\n469\t    witness that each conjunct is independently necessary, and\n470\t    `H_VestigialModeIsGraviton_at_one` witnesses that the bundle is\n471\t    satisfiable. -/\n472\tdef H_VestigialModeIsGraviton (χ_vest : ℝ) : Prop :=\n473\t  0 < χ_vest ∧\n474\t  LigoSatisfied (c_GW_deviation χ_vest) ∧\n475\t  |c_GW_deviation χ_vest| < 1 / 2\n476\t\n477\t/-- The natural anchor `χ_vest = 1` discharges the bundled hypothesis. -/\n478\ttheorem H_VestigialModeIsGraviton_at_one :\n479\t    H_VestigialModeIsGraviton 1 := by\n480\t  refine ⟨by norm_num, ligo_satisfied_at_chi_one, ?_⟩\n481\t  -- Δc/c at χ=1 is zero; |0| < 1/2.\n482\t  rw [c_GW_deviation, Real.sqrt_one]\n483\t  simp\n484\t\n485\t/-- **Falsifier A.** χ_vest = 1/10 (natural-range lower) fails P2. -/\n486\ttheorem H_VestigialModeIsGraviton_fails_at_natural_lower :\n487\t    ¬ H_VestigialModeIsGraviton chi_vest_natural_lower := by\n488\t  intro ⟨_, h2, _⟩\n489\t  exact natural_lower_violates_ligo h2\n490\t\n491\t/-- **Falsifier B.** χ_vest = 10 (natural-range upper) fails P2. -/\n492\ttheorem H_VestigialModeIsGraviton_fails_at_natural_upper :\n493\t    ¬ H_VestigialModeIsGraviton chi_vest_natural_upper := by\n494\t  intro ⟨_, h2, _⟩\n495\t  exact natural_upper_violates_ligo h2\n496\t\n497\t/-- **Falsifier C.** χ_vest = 0 fails P1 (positivity). -/\n498\ttheorem H_VestigialModeIsGraviton_fails_at_zero :\n499\t    ¬ H_VestigialModeIsGraviton 0 := by\n500\t  intro ⟨h1, _, _⟩\n501\t  exact lt_irrefl 0 h1\n502\t\n503\t/-- **Falsifier D — load-bearing for P3'.** χ_vest = 1/4 satisfies P1\n504\t    (positivity) but fails P3': `Δc/c = √(1/4) − 1 = −1/2`, so\n505\t    `|Δ| = 1/2`, violating `< 1/2`. Properties\n57\t\n58\tEach phase is characterized by the status of two order parameters:\n59\t- tetrad_vev: whether ⟨e^a_μ⟩ ≠ 0\n60\t- metric_nonzero: whether g_μν = η_ab ⟨E^a_μ E^b_ν⟩ ≠ 0\n61\t-/\n62\t\n63\t/-- Whether the tetrad VEV is nonzero in a given phase. -/\n64\tdef has_tetrad_vev : VestigialPhase → Bool\n65\t  | VestigialPhase.pre_geometric => false\n66\t  | VestigialPhase.vestigial => false\n67\t  | VestigialPhase.full_tetrad => true\n68\t\n69\t/-- Whether the metric correlator is nonzero in a given phase. -/\n70\tdef has_metric : VestigialPhase → exact absurd h (by decide)\n117\t  | VestigialPhase.vestigial => intro h; exact absurd h (by decide)\n118\t  | VestigialPhase.full_tetrad => intro _; rfl\n119\t\n120\t/-!\n121\t## Phase Hierarchy\n122\t\n123\tThe phases form a total order: pre_geometric < vestigial < full_tetrad.\n124\tThis corresponds to increasing symmetry breaking from SO(3,1) × SO(3,1).\n125\t-/\n126\t\n127\t/-- Numerical ordering of phases for comparison. -/\n128\tdef phase_order : VestigialPhase → Nat\n129\t  | VestigialPhase.pre_geometric => 0\n130\t  | VestigialPhase.vestigial => 1\n131\t  | VestigialPhase.full_tetrad => 2\n132\t\n133\t/-- **Phase hierarchy: pre_geometric < vestigial < full_tetrad.**\n134\t    This ordering reflects increasing symmetry breaking. -/\n135\ttheorem phase_hierarchy :\n136\t    phase_order VestigialPhase.pre_geometric < phase_order VestigialPhase.vestigial ∧\n137\t    phase_order VestigialPhase.vestigial < phase_order VestigialPhase.full_tetrad := by\n138\t  constructor <;> decide\n139\t\n140\t/-- Each phase has more structure than the previous one:\n141\t    if a property holds at level n, it also holds at level n+1.\n142\t    Specifically: metric in vestigial → metric in full_tetrad. -/\n143\ttheorem metric_monotone :\n144\t    has_metric VestigialPhase.vestigial = true →\n145\t    has_metric VestigialPhase.full_tetrad = true := by\n146\t  intro _; This\n178\tmeans bosonic and fermionic geodesics differ — a violation of the\n179\tEquivalence Principle.\n180\t\n181\tThe EP violation is quantified by the ratio:\n182\t    Delta_EP = 1 - <e^a_mu> / sqrt(<e^a_mu e^b_nu> eta_ab)\n183\t\n184\tIn the vestigial phase: Delta_EP = 1 (maximal violation).\n185\tIn the full tetrad phase: Delta_EP → 0 (EP restored).\n186\t-/\n187\t\n188\t/-- EP violation parameter: 1 in vestigial, 0 in full tetrad,\n189\t    undefined in pre-geometric (no metric exists). -/\n190\tnoncomputable def ep_violation (p : VestigialPhase) : Option ℝ :=\n191\t  match p with\n192\t  | VestigialPhase.pre_geometric => none  -- no metric, EP undefined\n193\t  | VestigialPhase.vestigial => some 1.0  -- maximal violation\n194\t  | VestigialPhase.full_tetrad => some 0.0  -- EP restored\n195\t\n196\t/-- **In the vestigial phase, EP violation is maximal.** -/\n197\ttheorem ep_violation_maximal_vestigial :\n198\t    ep_violation VestigialPhase.vestigial = some 1.0 := by rfl\n199\t\n200\t/-- **In the full tetrad phase, EP is restored.** -/\n201\ttheorem ep_violation_zero_full :\n202\t    ep_violation VestigialPhase.full_tetrad = some 0.0 := by rfl\n203\t\n204\t/-- **EP violation is a testable prediction: it distinguishes\n205\t    vestigial from full tetrad observationally.** -/\n206\ttheorem ep_distinguishes_phases :\n207\t    ep_violation VestigialPhase.vestigial ≠ ep_violation VestigialPhase.full_tetrad := by\n208\t  unfold ep_violation\n209\t  -- some 1.0 ≠ some 0.0\n210\t  intro h\n211\t  -- h : some 1.0 = some 0.0, extract the inner equality\n212\t  have : (1.0 : ℝ) = 0.0 := Option.some.inj h\n213\t  linarith\n214\t\n215\t/-!\n216\t## Sign Problem Severity\n217\t\n218\tThe Lorentzian theory has a sign problem: the auxiliary action is not\n219\tpositive-definite for timelike tetrad components. The average sign\n220\tdecays exponentially with lattice volume:\n221\t\n222\t    <sign> ~ exp(-f · L^d)\n223\t\n224\twhere f > 0 depends on the coupling. This means direct importance\n225\tsampling becomes exponentially expensive for large lattices.\n226\t-/\n227\t\n228\t/-- The sign problem severity grows with lattice volume.\n229\t    For a d-dimensional lattice of size L, the volume is L^d. -/\n230\tdef lattice_volume (L d : Nat) : Nat := L ^ d\n231\t\n232\t/-- Doubling L increases volume by factor 2^d. -/\n233\t-- PROVIDED SOLUTION: L^d * 2^d = (2L)^d by Nat.mul_pow\n234\ttheorem volume_doubles (L d : Nat) :\n235\t    lattice_volume (2 * L) d = 2 ^ d * lattice_volume L d := by\n236\t  unfold lattice_volume\n237\t  ring\n238\t\n239\t/-!\n240\t## Strengthening: Phase Hierarchy Quantification\n241\t-/\n242\t\n243\t/-- **The three phases form a total order on information content.**\n244\t    pre_geometric < vestigial < full_tetrad in terms of geometric structure. -/\n245\tdef phase_info_level : VestigialPhase → Nat\n246\t  | VestigialPhase.pre_geometric => 0\n247\t  | VestigialPhase.vestigial => 1\n248\t  | VestigialPhase.full_tetrad => 2\n249\t\n250\t/-- Phase levels are distinct. -/\n251\ttheorem phase_levels_distinct :\n252\t    phase_info_level VestigialPhase.pre_geometric ≠ phase_info_level VestigialPhase.vestigial ∧\n253\t    phase_info_level VestigialPhase.vestigial ≠ phase_info_level VestigialPhase.full_tetrad ∧\n254\t    phase_info_level VestigialPhase.pre_geometric ≠ phase_info_level VestigialPhase.full_tetrad := by\n255\t  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> decide\n256\t\n257\t/-- Phase levels are strictly ordered. -/\n258\ttheorem phase_levels_ordered :\n259\t    phase_info_level VestigialPhase.pre_geometric < phase_info_level VestigialPhase.vestigial ∧\n260\t    phase_info_level VestigialPhase.vestigial < phase_info_level VestigialPhase.full_tetrad := by\n261\t  constructor <;> decide\n262\t\n263\t/-- **The metric DOF count in the vestigial phase is d(d+1)/2.**\n264\t    In 4D this is 10 — the same number as in GR. {"parentUuid":"fc345ccb-dbb3-4221-96d5-6d2ee582a058","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"ad2aa620ea5ffe0d8","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01QFXffYWLCxBXmRvV1r2bza","type":"tool_result","content":"330\t\n331\t\\subsection{Vergeles unitarity propositions}\n332\t\n333\tThe one-loop calibration of $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{ADW}}$ to unity rests on three\n334\tVergeles structural propositions: positivity of the determinantal one-loop\n335\tcoefficient (\\texttt{LinearizedEFE.H\\_VergelesPositivity}),\n336\tcritical-limit collapse where $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{ADW}} \\to 1$ as the gap\n337\tcloses (\\texttt{LinearizedEFE.H\\_CriticalLimitCollapse}), and reduction\n338\tto the Adler closed form in the deep-gap regime\n339\t(\\texttt{LinearizedEFE.H\\_DeepGapReducesToAdler}). All three are\n340\ttracked-hypothesis Props in the current draft; the explicit one-loop\n341\tcalculation that discharges them is open and is reported as such in\n342\t\\S\\ref{sec:linearized-efe}.\n343\t\n344\t\\subsection{Phase diagram}\n345\t\n346\tThe phase diagram in the $(N_f,\\Lambda_{\\mathrm{UV}})$ plane has the\n347\ttetrad-condensed phase along the upper-left wedge bounded by the\n348\t$G = G_c^{\\mathrm{ADW}}$ critical line. Naturalness of the ultraviolet\n349\tmatching to the Planck scale fixes\n350\t$\\Lambda_{\\mathrm{UV}}\\sim M_{\\mathrm{Pl}}\\simeq 1.2\\times 10^{19}\\,\\mathrm{GeV}$.\n351\tAnomaly-cancellation in the chirality-wall sector (Bundles D2 and L2) and\n352\tmodular invariance of the SM partition function together fix\n353\t$N_f = 16$ as the unique consistent count. The single point\n354\t$(\\Lambda_{\\mathrm{UV}},N_f) = (M_{\\mathrm{Pl}},16)$ is the natural\n355\tmicroscopic point at which all subsequent\n356\t\\eqref{eq:sakharov-identity}-driven predictions are evaluated.\n357\t\n358\t\\paragraph{Same scale, six observables.}\n359\t\\eqref{eq:adw-gap} is the operational definition of $\\Lambda_{\\mathrm{UV}}$.\n360\tSubsequent sections feed the same $\\Lambda_{\\mathrm{UV}}$ into Newton's\n361\tconstant (\\S\\ref{sec:linearized-efe}), the BCH regime-partition mass\n362\t$M_c$ (\\S\\ref{sec:bch-four-laws}), the BH-entropy logarithmic-correction\n363\tprefactor through the Kaul--Majumdar count (\\S\\ref{sec:bh-entropy}), the\n364\temergent cosmological constant\n365\t$\\Lambda_{\\mathrm{emerg}}$ (\\S\\ref{sec:cc-emergent}), and the\n366\tEinstein--Cartan torsion amplitude $|T_{\\mathrm{EC}}|$\n367\t(\\S\\ref{sec:einstein-cartan}). One scale, six observables, no additional\n368\tfree dial.\n369\t\n370\t\n371\t%% =====================================================================\n372\t%% §3 — Gauge erasure: only U(1) survives the fluid layer\n373\t%% Lift: paper3_gauge_erasure\n374\t%% =====================================================================\n375\t\n376\t\\figuredeferred{fig:d3-adw-bifurcation}{the tetrad-gap bifurcation diagram; \\texttt{adw/} solves the gap equation but the bifurcation sweep is a separate production run that has not been made}\n377\t\\section{Gauge erasure: only $U(1)$ survives the fluid layer}\n378\t\\label{sec:gauge-erasure}\n379\t\n380\tA higher-form-symmetry analysis of Glorioso--Liu Schwinger--Keldysh effective\n381\tfield theory~\\cite{GloriosoLiu2018} establishes that the hydrodynamic layer\n382\t\\emph{erases} non-Abelian one-form gauge symmetry: only $U(1)$ survives the\n383\tfluid-cell coarse-graining as a continuous one-form, with non-Abelian\n384\tgauge fields surviving only as discrete centre symmetries that re-enter\n385\tthrough the deconfinement transition (\\S\\ref{sec:confinement}). The erasure\n386\ttheorem (Lean: \\texttt{GaugeErasure.gauge\\_erasure} +\n387\t\\texttt{GaugeErasure.u1\\_survival}) is the\n388\t\\emph{first} of three predictive-boundary cuts that force the ADW route\n389\tto the tetrad-condensation channel."}]},"uuid":"4e34d177-4113-4699-a298-ce786f5f99fb","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:37:22.250Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"fc345ccb-dbb3-4221-96d5-6d2ee582a058","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

Transplanting that identification\n623\tonto the ADW substrate --- whose metric-channel susceptibility we\n624\tcompute independently, and which does not fix $\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}$\n625\t--- yields the leading-order relation\n626\t\\begin{equation}\n627\t\\label{eq:c-gw-leading}\n628\tc_{\\mathrm{GW}}(\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}) \\;=\\; c\\,\\sqrt{\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}}\\,,\n629\t\\qquad \\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}} \\in [0.1,\\,10] \\text{ (natural range)}.\n630\t\\end{equation}\n631\t\\noindent\n632\tEq.~\\eqref{eq:c-gw-leading} is ours, not Volovik's: on his own\n633\tde~Sitter two-fluid background the Landau formula returns $s_2 = c$\n634\texactly --- structurally, from the stiff-matter equation of state ---\n635\twhich corresponds to $\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}} = 1$. The\n636\t$\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}$-dependence enters only through our substrate.\n637\t\\noindent\n638\tClosed in \\texttt{GravitationalWaves.c\\_GW\\_at\\_chi\\_one}, the prediction\n639\tagrees with general relativity ($c_{\\mathrm{GW}}=c$) only at\n640\t$\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}=1$\n641\t(\\texttt{GravitationalWaves.c\\_GW\\_deviation\\_zero\\_iff\\_chi\\_one}),\n642\tand is strictly monotone in $\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}$\n643\t(\\texttt{c\\_GW\\_deviation\\_strict\\_mono}). The natural range of\n644\t$\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}$ is a \\emph{project-adopted} order-unity\n645\tnaturalness window ($\\pm 1$ decade about the unit-normalised\n646\trandom-phase-approximation bubble-integral scale\n647\t$\\mathcal{O}(\\Lambda_{\\mathrm{UV}}^{2}/16\\pi^{2})$, the same\n648\tconvention as the $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{ADW}}\\in[0.1,10]$ prior of\n649\t\\S\\ref{sec:linearized-efe}); it is a modeling choice of this\n650\tproject, not a published derivation. Physically, the lower edge marks\n651\tthe critical-fluid regime ($\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}\\sim 0.1$, where\n652\tvestigial-condensate susceptibility is well-defined) and the upper\n653\tedge the strong-coupling regime ($\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}\\sim 10$,\n654\tbeyond which the ADW one-loop expansion fails).\n655\t\n656\t\\subsection{LIGO--Virgo cap and falsification}\n657\t\n658\tThe LIGO--Virgo joint observation of GW170817 with the\n659\tGRB~170817A counterpart constrains the gravitational-wave speed\n660\tasymmetrically,\n661\t$-3\\times 10^{-15} \\le \\Delta c/c \\le\n662\t+7\\times 10^{-16}$~\\cite{Abbott2017GW170817}; throughout we adopt the\n663\tconservative two-sided envelope $|\\Delta c/c| \\le 3\\times 10^{-15}$\n664\t(the looser, negative side) as the constraint cap. Combined\n665\twith~\\eqref{eq:c-gw-leading}, the natural range produces\n666\t$\\Delta c/c$ sweeping $[-0.68, +2.16]$, vanishing only at\n667\t$\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}} = 1$ and violating the LIGO--Virgo cap by\n668\troughly fourteen orders of magnitude at the endpoints. Lean\n669\t\\texttt{GravitationalWaves.natural\\_lower\\_violates\\_ligo} and\n670\t\\texttt{natural\\_upper\\_violates\\_ligo} discharge the two endpoint\n671\tfalsifiers, and \\texttt{vestigial\\_natural\\_range\\_violates\\_ligo}\n672\tbundles them; the endpoint theorem\n673\t\\texttt{natural\\_endpoints\\_violate\\_ligo\\_window} adds that no\n674\trescaling of $c$ rescues either endpoint. None of these is a statement\n675\tabout the interior: $\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}} = 1$ satisfies the cap\n676\t(\\texttt{ligo\\_satisfied\\_at\\_chi\\_one}), and the compatible window is\n677\tnested strictly \\emph{inside} the natural range\n678\t(\\texttt{ligo\\_window\\_subset\\_natural\\_range}), meeting it there\n679\t(\\texttt{ligo\\_window\\_inter\\_natural\\_range\\_nonempty}).\n680\t\n681\tWhat GW170817 delivers over the natural range is therefore a\n682\tconfinement, not a universal exclusion. For non-negative\n683\t$\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}$ satisfying the cap,\n684\t\\begin{equation}\n685\t(1-\\tau)^2 \\;\\le\\; \\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}} \\;\\le\\; (1+\\tau)^2,\n686\t\\qquad \\tau = 3\\times 10^{-15},\n687\t\\end{equation}\n688\t\\noindent\n689\tand hence $0.1 < \\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}} < 10$ strictly --- theorem\n690\t\\texttt{ligo\\_confines\\_chi\\_vest\\_within\\_natural\\_range} (zero\n691\t\\texttt{sorry}). The admissible interval has width exactly $4\\tau$\n692\t(\\texttt{ligo\\_window\\_width\\_eq}) against the natural range's $9.9$\n693\t(\\texttt{natural\\_range\\_width\\_eq}), a ratio of more than fourteen\n694\torders of magnitude\n695\t(\\texttt{ligo\\_window\\_width\\_lt\\_natural\\_range\\_width\\_by\\_1e14}).\n696\tThat ratio is the load-bearing fine-tuning claim.\n697\t\n698\tThree routes could supply a mechanism that makes the surviving locus\n699\tstructural rather than tuned, and each would reopen the vestigial\n700\tchannel that \\S\\ref{sec:closure-triad} otherwise closes: (i) a\n701\tsymmetry-driven fixed point making $\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}} = 1$ exact\n702\tunder the RG flow; (ii) a distinct metric-channel identification in\n703\twhich the ``vestigial mode'' is not the second-sound degree of freedom\n704\tat all; and (iii) a\n705\tfrequency-dependent $\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}$ at higher derivative order.\n706\tBundle~L1 develops all three, and all three remain open. On route (iii),\n707\t\\texttt{vestigial\\_dispersion\\_below\\_ligo\\_at\\_inspiral\\_peak} shows\n708\tthe SK-EFT dispersion correction stays inside the GW170817 tolerance\n709\t\\emph{conditional on} $|\\gamma| \\leq 10^{-30}$ --- a Phase~6a scaffold\n710\tvalue, neither derived nor measured, which the theorem takes as a\n711\thypothesis rather than establishes. A placeholder-sized correction\n712\twould therefore not relax the constraint; a larger one is not excluded.\n713\tRoutes (i) and (ii) are the Phase~6 targets.\n714\t\n715\t\\subsection{Architecture: triad closure}\n716\t\n717\t\\S\\ref{sec:gw170817} is the third of the predictive-boundary closures of\n718\t\\S\\ref{sec:closure-triad}. It is reported here in full because the\n719\tconstraint is load-bearing for the remaining argument: the vestigial\n720\tgraviton survives GW170817 only at a fine-tuned\n721\t$\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}} = 1$, so absent a mechanism that pins it there,\n722\tthe substrate's gravity-emergence channel is forced to the ADW route.\n723\tThe closure is therefore conditional on the absence of such a\n724\tmechanism, not on an outright exclusion --- \\S\\ref{sec:gw170817} states\n725\tthe three recovery paths that would supply one. Bundle~L1 ships the same content as a\n726\tfour-page Physical Review Letters splash; the same numerical anchors are\n727\tshared. The \\texttt{VestigialGravity} module supplements with the\n728\tphase-count theorem (\\texttt{phase\\_count}) showing that only\n729\tthe full-tetrad phase admits classical gravity, while the\n730\tvestigial phase has metric structure but no tetrad\n731\t(\\texttt{vestigial\\_has\\_metric\\_no\\_tetrad}), generating the Equivalence-Principle\n732\tviolation that distinguishes vestigial from full\n733\t(\\texttt{wep\\_distinguishes\\_vestigial\\_from\\_full}).\n734\t\n735\t\\subsection{Dispersive correction (forward link to \\S\\ref{sec:vestigial-mc})}\n736\t\n737\tThe leading-order $c_{\\mathrm{GW}} = c\\sqrt{\\chi_{\\mathrm{vest}}}$ constraint\n738\talready confines the natural range to a window of width $4\\tau$. No $L = 6$\n997\tensemble exists. The $L = 8$, $m = 0.1$ ensemble is a null\n1016\tresult: no signal above statistical noise.\n1017\t\n1018\tThe two order parameters named above, $|\\langle\\chi\\rangle|$ and\n1019\t$\\det(e^a_\\mu)$, are \\emph{not} among the observables the current ensembles\n1020\trecord -- the stored histories are $h^2$, $\\Delta H$, $\\mathrm{tr}\\,m^2$ and\n1021\t$\\mathrm{tr}\\,Q^2$ -- so no histogram in either order parameter can be formed\n1022\tfrom the existing data, and no transition coupling can be compared against\n1023\t$G_c^{\\mathrm{ADW}}$. The $m \\to 0$ ensemble set and the Binder-cumulant and\n1024\tconnected-susceptibility detectors are prerequisites for any such statement;\n1025\tsee the deferral note below.\n1026\t\n1027\t\\subsection{$L \\ge 8$ convergence: in flight}\n1028\t\n1029\tAt $L = 8$ the autocorrelation time grows; convergence at $L = 8$ requires\n1030\teither a longer Markov chain or a Berges--Sexty-type complex-Langevin\n1031\tacceleration~\\cite{BergesSexty2008}. Conditional on RHMC convergence, this is the\n1048\tsubstrate's first quantitative empirical anchor for emergent gravity.\n1049\t\n1050\t\n1051\t%% =====================================================================\n1052\t%% §11 — Scalar rung: Higgs identification + microscopic m_H\n1053\t%% Lift: paper20_scalar_rung\n1054\t%% =====================================================================\n1055\t\n1056\t\\figuredeferred{fig:d3-vestigial-mc}{the lattice Monte-Carlo phase diagram; blocked on the $m\\to0$ production set, which the $L=8$, $m=0.1$ run showed is required before any signal is visible}\n1057\t\\section{Matter rungs: scalar and Majorana}\n1058\t\\label{sec:scalar-rung}\n1059\t\n1060\tThe Wetterich--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) scalar\n1061\tchannel~\\cite{Wetterich1990} of the ADW substrate identifies the Higgs\n1062\tboson as a Higgs-bilinear composite of the four-fermion contact channel\n1063\tthat drove the gap equation of \\S\\ref{sec:adw-gap}. {"parentUuid":"bc90106e-de19-4b87-9347-65bcf03ddb20","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"ad2aa620ea5ffe0d8","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Vak63YZFqEGJzS5zZv2CSa","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tWe discuss the two-step transitions in superconductors, where the intermediate state between the Cooper pair state and the normal metal is the 4-fermion condensate, which is called the intertwined vestigial order. We discuss different types of the vestigial order, which are possible in the spin-triplet superfluid 3 He, and the topological objects in the vestigial phases. Since in 3 He the order parameter $${{A}_{{\\alpha i}}}$$ represents the analog of gravitational tetrads, we suggest that the vestigial states are possible in quantum gravity. As in superconductors, the fermionic vacuum can experience two consequent phase transitions. At first transition the metric appears as the bilinear combination of tetrads $${{g}_{{\\mu \\nu }}} = {{\\eta }_{{ab}}}\\langle \\hat {E}_{\\mu }^{a}\\hat {E}_{\\nu }^{b}\\rangle $$ , while the tetrad order parameter is still absent, $$e_{\\mu }^{a} = \\langle \\hat {E}_{\\mu }^{a}\\rangle = 0$$ . This corresponds to the bosonic Einstein general relativity, which emerges in the fermionic vacuum. The nonzero tetrads $$e_{\\mu }^{a} = \\langle \\hat {E}_{\\mu }^{a}\\rangle \\ne 0$$ appear at the second transition, where a kind of the Einstein–Cartan–Sciama–Kibble tetrad gravity is formed. This suggests that on the levels of particles, gravity acts with different strength on fermions and bosons.\n2\t"}]},"uuid":"61220150-127b-4132-bbf2-ac3b8102b3cc","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:39:07.767Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"bc90106e-de19-4b87-9347-65bcf03ddb20","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

],\n64\t    \"published-print\": {\n65\t      \"date-parts\": [\n66\t        [\n67\t          2024,\n68\t          2\n69\t        ]\n70\t      ]\n71\t    },\n72\t    \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>We discuss the two-step transitions in superconductors, where the intermediate state between the Cooper pair state and the normal metal is the 4-fermion condensate, which is called the intertwined vestigial order. We discuss different types of the vestigial order, which are possible in the spin-triplet superfluid <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>He, and the topological objects in the vestigial phases. Since in <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>He the order parameter <jats:inline-formula><jats:tex-math>$${{A}_{{\\\\alpha i}}}$$</jats:tex-math></jats:inline-formula> represents the analog of gravitational tetrads, we suggest that the vestigial states are possible in quantum gravity. As in superconductors, the fermionic vacuum can experience two consequent phase transitions. At first transition the metric appears as the bilinear combination of tetrads <jats:inline-formula><jats:tex-math>$${{g}_{{\\\\mu \\\\nu }}} = {{\\\\eta }_{{ab}}}\\\\langle \\\\hat {E}_{\\\\mu }^{a}\\\\hat {E}_{\\\\nu }^{b}\\\\rangle $$</jats:tex-math></jats:inline-formula>, while the tetrad order parameter is still absent, <jats:inline-formula><jats:tex-math>$$e_{\\\\mu }^{a} = \\\\langle \\\\hat {E}_{\\\\mu }^{a}\\\\rangle = 0$$</jats:tex-math></jats:inline-formula>. This corresponds to the bosonic Einstein general relativity, which emerges in the fermionic vacuum. The nonzero tetrads <jats:inline-formula><jats:tex-math>$$e_{\\\\mu }^{a} = \\\\langle \\\\hat {E}_{\\\\mu }^{a}\\\\rangle \\\\ne 0$$</jats:tex-math></jats:inline-formula> appear at the second transition, where a kind of the Einstein\\u2013Cartan\\u2013Sciama\\u2013Kibble tetrad gravity is formed. This suggests that on the levels of particles, gravity acts with different strength on fermions and bosons.</jats:p>\",\n73\t    \"DOI\": \"10.1134/s002136402460006x\",\n74\t    \"type\": \"journal-article\",\n75\t    \"created\": {\n76\t      \"date-parts\": [\n77\t        [\n78\t          2024,\n79\t          2,\n80\t          12\n81\t        ]\n82\t      ],\n83\t      \"date-time\": \"2024-02-12T18:02:45Z\",\n84\t      \"timestamp\": 1707760965000\n85\t    },\n86\t    \"page\": \"330-334\",\n87\t    \"update-policy\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/springer_crossmark_policy\",\n88\t    \"source\": \"Crossref\",\n89\t    \"is-referenced-by-count\": 5,\n90\t    \"title\": [\n91\t      \"Fermionic Quartet and Vestigial Gravity\"\n92\t    ],\n93\t    \"prefix\": \"10.1134\",\n94\t    \"volume\": \"119\",\n95\t    \"author\": [\n96\t      {\n97\t        \"given\": \"G.
